conviction_note: The Q3 numbers are new, so the move is sized at 5.5%, above the name's own median print-day move of about 4% and below the 7% base. This is because the guide is very unlikely to change in a Q3 release, and the stock now carries a CVC take-private premium that cushions both a miss and a beat. p_up is 48 because the evidence offsets: the CEO said in July he was comfortable with Q3, and shorts are about 3.4% of the shares (roughly 12% of the free float). Against that, the stock fell on 3 of its 4 real prints, including two that were in line or beat, and a +28% 20-day run-up holds a bid premium that management cannot confirm. The findings sum to +0.5 and the scaled number is -0.2. The sign gap is small: the findings lean on squeeze fuel, while the scaled number leans on a reaction history of selling prints.

CEO Austin Lally to Nyhetsbyrån Direkt: comfortable with how the year will end, based on Q3 trading so far; consumers still uncertain

new_in_release.expect: Q3 ARR, adjusted EBIT, attrition and CPA are not pre-released. Expect in line to slightly above the company guide: the CEO was comfortable with Q3 in July, and DNB Carnegie said adjusted EBIT beat in each listed quarter. There is no sourced consensus.
The 2026 outlook is most likely reiterated (H1 EBIT margin 26.7% vs the >26% guide). The FY2027 guide is not due until the Feb 2027 report, so a guidance change is unlikely.
FCF is the line the market has doubted (Ålandsbanken, Feb 2026). Expect a fourth positive quarter, but the size is unknown.
First management comment since the FT's 21 Oct report of CVC interest and the Apple home-security launch of about 7 Oct. Default is 'no comment on speculation'; the direction is unknown.

findings.finding: On 30 Jul the CEO said Q3 trading made him comfortable with how 2026 ends, and the outlook (ARR growth about 10% ex Mexico, EBIT margin >26%) was confirmed. That points to an in-line or slightly better Q3 inside the guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: In-line prints have been sold: Q2 2026 was 'very close to estimates' and fell 4.1%; FY25 beat adjusted EBIT and fell 16.4% (DNB Carnegie: 'not a -16% report'); Q1 2026 rose 4.0%; Q3'25 -0.3%.
findings.original_quote: “Det vi har sagt i dag är att vi bekräftar utsikterna för 2026, och när jag ser på utvecklingen under tredje kvartalet känner jag mig trygg med hur året kommer att sluta” (We confirm the 2026 outlook, and looking at Q3 trading I feel comfortable with how the year will end)
findings.why_not_priced: It is largely priced: the statement is public and sits inside the guide. What is left is the small chance that 'comfortable' means a beat. If the market fully believed one, the stock would have rerated on fundamentals before the bid rumour. Instead it fell from 10.89 to 7.70 between 30 Jul and 8 Oct.
findings.independence: DNB Carnegie (13 Feb 2026) said Verisure beat adjusted EBIT in both of its listed quarters at that point: https://www.efn.se/dnb-carnegie-om-verisure-utmanar-uppfattningen-om-trygg-hamn

findings.finding: The FT reported on 21 Oct that CVC is at a very early stage of assessing a take-private bid (stock +10.0% on 22 Oct on 7.2m shares). Verisure has filed nothing on the Nasdaq Nordic feed since, and the Q3 call is management's first public appearance since the leak. Under MAR a sufficiently accurate leak of talks the issuer was party to would usually force a disclosure, so the silence suggests the company itself is not in talks. That leaves the premium (about 9.36 to 10.46) exposed to a 'no comment'.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: One observation: the leak itself was +10.0% on 22 Oct, and the ADT read-across added +5.0% (29 Oct) and +3.4% (30 Oct).
findings.original_quote: Financial Times skriver att CVC:s intresse för Verisure ska befinna sig i ett tidigt skede och det inte finns några garantier för en affär (the FT writes that CVC's interest is at an early stage and there is no guarantee of a deal)
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced, in the other direction. The 20-day run-up of +27.7% holds a bid premium, which is the market saying a bid is plausible. What the price does not show is that the issuer has filed nothing. If the market had read that silence as 'no talks with the company', the stock would have given back the 22 Oct gap instead of extending it to 10.86 on 30 Oct. The inference is mine; it is not a document.
findings.independence: Placera/Direkt, 21 Oct 20:24: CVC, Verisure and H&F declined to comment (https://www.placera.se/telegram/verisure-cvc-overvager-bud-pa-bolaget-20261021). The Nasdaq Nordic feed shows no Verisure release after 30 Sep.

findings.finding: Thrive Holdings (Apollo-financed) agreed on 29 Oct to buy ADT, the US alarm peer, for $15.3bn EV, $10 a share in cash, a 45.6% premium. That sets a sector take-private benchmark beside the CVC rumour, and Barclays notes peers trade or are bought at 2.5-5x ARR against Verisure's 3.5x.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Verisure rose 5.0% on 29 Oct and 3.4% on 30 Oct after the ADT announcement.
findings.original_quote: Thrive Holdings köper säkerhetsbolaget ADT i en kontantaffär med ett bolagsvärde på 15,3 miljarder dollar ... Aktieägarna erbjuds 10 dollar per aktie, motsvarande en premie på 45,6 procent
findings.why_not_priced: It is almost fully priced: the stock moved about 8.6% over two sessions. The residual is only that the print gives analysts a fresh ARR base to re-mark a take-private multiple against.
findings.independence: Barclays via EFN, 22 Oct: peers valued or acquired at 2.5-5x ARR, Verisure at 3.5x (https://efn.se/budrykte-lyfter-verisure-analytiker-inte-forvanade)

findings.finding: Disclosed short interest is 3.41% of capital (FI, 28 Oct), roughly 12% of a free float of about 30%. It came down from 3.65% on 13 Oct, so shorts covered slightly into the print. That leaves squeeze fuel under any print or call that keeps the bid alive.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print with this short level. Earlier public shorts (QRT, Marshall Wace) were 0.5-0.7% and had closed by July.
findings.original_quote: Summa procent 3,41 ... MILLENNIUM INTERNATIONAL MANAGEMENT LP 0,51 2026-10-12
findings.why_not_priced: The baseline's priced_lean already credits a +2.0 squeeze component. The residual is the float arithmetic the register does not show: 3.4% of capital is about four times larger as a share of tradable float. If that were fully priced, shorts would have covered harder after the bid leak; instead only 0.24pp came off.
findings.independence: Börskollen/Finwire, 13 Oct: total shorted 3.65%, Millennium the only public short (https://www.borskollen.se/nyheter/28/millennium-blir-forsta-publika-blankaren-i-verisure). Free-float arithmetic from the shareholder list (H&F 43.7%, Eiffel/GIC 16.0%, Alba 6.3%, Securholds 5.4%, management about 3%): https://valueandopportunity.com/2026/10/28/verisure-and-swiss-marketplace-two-more-busted-ipos-worth-a-second-glance/

findings.finding: The stock fell 6.2% on 7 Oct, which DNB Carnegie tied to an Apple home-security product launch, a competitive overhang. The Q3 call is management's first chance to answer it with attrition and new-installation data.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: One observation: -6.2% on 7 Oct and -1.6% the next day, then recovered within a week.
findings.original_quote: Under onsdagen förra veckan föll larmbolaget Verisure med drygt 6 procent ... Analyshuset DNB Carnegie kopplar det till en Apple-lansering
findings.why_not_priced: The 7 Oct fall is in the price, and Q3 data (to 30 Sep) predate the launch, so the numbers cannot show any effect. The only open question is whether management's framing on the call removes the overhang. I sized it small because a rebuttal by management is the expected case and may be ignored.

outside_window.finding: The 365-day lock-up for board and senior management expired around October 2026, and the post-Q3 trading window opens after the release. Insider sales would land after 3 Nov.
Arlo, Verisure's camera supplier, reports Q3 in early November. Nordea cut its Arlo-related sales expectations on 12 Oct. Expected after the window.
Whether CVC makes a formal approach. No dated deadline exists: Verisure is English-incorporated and outside the UK Takeover Code, so there is no put-up-or-shut-up date.

baseline_tension: The findings mostly agree with the mild positive lean (+0.66, driven by the short-squeeze component). They cut against the +27.7% 20-day run-up only through the bid-premium finding, which says some of that run-up rests on an approach the issuer has not confirmed.
language_note: The Swedish issuer feed and MFN calendar (Kvartalsrapport 2026-Q3, 2026-11-03 08:00) carried the only confirmation of the date and time; English searches returned only an estimated date.
The CEO's Q3 comfort statement exists only in a Swedish Nyhetsbyrån Direkt interview (placera.se). It is not in the English release.
Short-register detail (aggregate 3.65% on 13 Oct to 3.41% on 28 Oct; Millennium as the only public holder) came from FI and Börskollen/Finwire in Swedish; no English source carried it.
The Apple-launch explanation for the 7 Oct fall (DNB Carnegie via EFN) and the Barclays 2.5-5x ARR peer-multiple comment were found only in Swedish press.
The CVC story itself was FT/Reuters in English first; the Swedish wires added only that all parties declined to comment.
lessons_applied: 'A finding inside what the company already guided is a reported-quarter item the market was told to expect': CEO Q3 comfort finding cut from +0.3 to +0.2.

'You were right about the number and too small about the move; let the reaction history move p_up, not abs_move_pct': abs_move_pct raised from 5.0 to 5.5. The 3-of-4 selling history stays in p_up (48) only.

'In a live bid, results are noise': checked and not applied as a veto. Verisure is not in an offer period (early-stage rumour, no approach disclosed), so results still matter. This is why the bid-premium finding is kept at its own size rather than dropped or scaled up.
